sentences.text: Nakanectes bradti is a short-necked elasmosaurid plesiosaur distinguished by possessing a neck with only 39 to 42 cervical vertebrae, a count much shorter than in most other members of its group.
The genus name honors the Nakona people, also known as the Assiniboine, while the species name bradti commemorates the fossil hunter David Bradt.
The fossil was discovered in November 2010 by hunter David Bradt at the Charles M. Russell National Wildlife Refuge in Montana, United States.
Unfortunately, the specimen was partially destroyed by flooding before it could be fully recovered in 2011.
Researchers determined that Nakonanectes is a styxosaurine that exhibits convergent evolution with the South American Aristonectinae.
Nakanectes is classified within the class Reptilia as an elasmosaurid plesiosaur belonging to the family Elasmosauridae and the parent group Elasmosaurinae.
Found in the Bearpaw Formation, Nakonanectes lived during the late Campanian to early Maastrichtian in the Western Interior Seaway, specifically between 72.2 and 66 million years ago.
The presence of short-necked elasmosaurids in both North and South America suggests that this trait evolved independently in multiple locations.
